texts.facts: 1 2. Appellant/ wife herein was the complainant and respondent is the husband herein before Ld. Trial Court. In order to avoid any confusion, both the parties will be referred with the same nomenclature with which they were referred before Ld. Trial Court, in my subsequent paragraphs. 3. The brief facts necessary for disposal of present appeal are as follows :- " That the complainant was married to respondent No.1 as per Sikh customs and rites on 02.05.2004 at Tilak Nagar, New Delhi in which all the relatives from both sides were present. This was second marriage for both parties. That the parents of the complainant spent a huge amount in this marriage including Gold ornaments to the respondents and to the applicant. The ornaments of the complainant were taken by the respondent no. 1 which were weighing about 7 tolas and the same were pledged by the respondent no. 1 & 2 without giving any money to CA No. 265/2025 Charanpreet Kaur vs. Parvinder Singh & anr. Page no. 2 of 19 the complainant. That first three years after the marriage, everything was normal however the sisters of respondent no. 1 continued their interference in the married life of the complainant. That out of this wedlock two children are born, one daughter Mandeep Kaur now aged 17 years who is a student of class 12th and one son Gurkeerat Singh now aged 14 years who is student of class 9. That the respondents and their relatives have been continuously causing physical and mental torture to the complainant with the motive to throw her out of the matrimonial house which is a rented premises at present. That in the process of physical and mental torture to the complainant, Harpal Singh son of Harvinder Kaur sister of Respondent No. 1 and Ashmir son of Harjit Kaur who is also sister of respondent no. 1 join the respondents in beatings to the complainant and her life has been made miserable by the respondents. That even son of the complainant on the provocation of respondents has beaten the complainant a number of times and the respondents have motive to throw the complainant out of the house with her daughter who is the only support to the complainant. That In the year March. -April 2017, the complainant was beaten, the PCR call was made and the complainant including the respondents and sister of respondent no.1 were taken to Jungpura Police chowki where the matter was sorted out by the police and the respondents were warned not to cause to physical and mental torture to the complainant. That the respondents used to pick quarrel whenever they got chance on petty issues with the complainant and she has been subjected to continuous mental and physical torture by the respondents even the complainant has to remain hungry on several occasions when nothing is left for her food in the house. That on 17 March 2020 the respondent picked-up quarrel with the complainant and to save her life she had to leave the house with CA No. 265/2025 Charanpreet Kaur vs. Parvinder Singh & anr. Page no. 3 of 19 her children and she remained in her parental house for about 3 months only thereafter she was allowed to enter the house. That on the occasion of Diwali last year (2021) the respondent no. 2 had gone to her daughter's place and when the children wanted to celebrate diwali with light and crackers, the respondent no. 1 removed all the electrical connections for lighting in the house and threatened the complainant and the children that Diwali cannot be celebrated without presence of respondent no. That the respondents have purchased two flats, one single room set and one two room set above the Modi Bakery opposite Kashmiri Park, Jungpura Bhogal in the name of respondent no. 2, the respondents are getting rent from tenants of both the flats. But at the same time they are not providing any money to the complainant for house hold requirements. That the respondents now have only motive to throw the complainant and her daughter from the house and they have been making conspiracy by putting false allegations of theft on the complainant. That on date 17.04.2022, when the complainant was physically assaulted by the respondent no. 1 and his nephews, call was made 112 number, all were taken to police chowki Jungpura where police left the respondents and their relatives by giving warning since this matter. That on 19.05.2022 again false allegation of theft were put against the complainant and she was beaten by respondents and were pushing out the complainant out of the house for which police complaint has been made. That the life of the complainant is made hell, she is not even allowed to go room of her husband who stays with his mother during the night time. Which is having facility of air-conditioning. Even the daughter of the complainant is not allowed to use that room. That the complainant has come to know that respondent no 1 is having illicit relation with other CA No. 265/2025 Charanpreet Kaur vs. Parvinder Singh & anr. Page no. 4 of 19 women and living a lavish life style whereas the complainant under compelling circumstances is working in Kirana shop on a petty salary of Rs 7,000/- per month to meet her medical expenses. That the respondents have continuously caused physical and mental torture to the complainant with any reason or rhyme. That the respondent No.1 is gainfully self employed earning about Rs. 50,000/- per month and also has rental income, which is approx R$40,000/- Rs50,000/- per month. The respondent No.1 is legally bound to provide maintenance to the complainant and their daughter." GROUNDS OF APPEAL 5. Feeling aggrieved by the impugned order dated 30.06.2025 passed by Ld. Trial Court, respondent/ husband has challenged the said order by way of present appeal on the following grounds :- A. That, the impugned judgement / order dated 30.06.2025 is contrary to the law, facts and circumstances of the case. B. That, the maintenance amount Rs. 10,000/- per month awarded to the wife / appellant is not reasonable and realistic which is very less and appellant cannot meet the monthly expenses. The net income of husband / respondent No. has been Charanpreet Kaur vs Parvinder Singh on 7 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127053166/ 3 assessed by this honorable court is Rs.50,000/-per CA No. 265/2025 Charanpreet Kaur vs. Parvinder Singh & anr. Page no. 5 of 19 month, out of which the income of the respondent no.l is divided into five portions wherein only one portion/share of his income ie. allotted to month Rs. 10,000/-per appellant/complainant (inclusive of food, clothing, shelter, education and health her expenses are Rs. 35,000/-per month. The ad-interim maintenance of Rs. 4,000/- being granted to the daughter by respondent no. 1 has been stopped by respondent No.1 after passing the above said impugned interim maintenance order which the trial court overlooked. C. That, the trial court failed to consider the serious ill health of the appellant and appellant herself is suffering from brain disorder and getting regular fits which requires constant care and frequent expenditure. D. That, great prejudice has been caused to the appellant/ complainant as she has been forced to pay the rent of approx. Rs. 15,000/- per month as per the interim order which suggests that Rs. 10,000/- per month (Rupee Ten thousand only) be paid to the complainant/appellant including food, clothing, shelter, education and health per month. E. That, the appellant/complainant is also burdened with the maintenance, food, clothing, shelter, and health etc. of the daughter, as the ad- interim maintenance of Rs. 4,000/- being paid to the daughter by the respondent no, 1 has been stopped by him after passing the above said impugned interim maintenance order and the daughter is studying in B. Com final year and also taking computer classes. She is unmarried and has no source of income. F. That the physical condition of the appellant has worsened due to deteriorating health condition of the appellant. There is none in the household except daughter at present to look after the appellant and both have to look after each other. As such, the appellant have landed into clinical depression and anxiety. G. That the appellant/ complainant cannot meet the expenses of the rental house as no house in the Jangpura/Bhogal (1 BHK) locality is less than Rs. 15,000/- per month and security deposit approximately Rs. 30,000/- equals to 2 months' rent. Monthly rent is excluding water and electricity bills which CA No. 265/2025 Charanpreet Kaur vs. Parvinder Singh & anr. Page no. 6 of 19 will be as per usage per month. H. That the respondent no.1 & 2 are bound to provide shared household/matrimonial home to the appellant/ complainant in the property no. 3/31, First floor, Double Storey, DDA Flats, Near Mother Dairy, Opp. Kashmiri Park, Jangpura Extension, Bhogal, New Delhi - 110014 where respondent no1 along with respondent no 2 and his son has shifted, as the appellant being his legally wedded wife and the daughter born out of the said wedlock. Case No.1055/2022. L. That, in these circumstances, it is beseeched from this Hon'ble Court to alter the judgement / order dated 30.06.2025, to an extent that wife/ appellant should not be burdened with the maintenance of daughter and shelter as well as should not be forced to pay the rent of approx.. 15000/- per month as per the interim order and shared household/matrimonial home is provided by the respondent no.1 in property No. 3/31, First floor, Double Storey, DDA Flats, Near Mother Dairy, Opp. Kashmiri Park, Jangpura CA No. 265/2025 Charanpreet Kaur vs. Parvinder Singh & anr. Page no. 7 of 19 Extension, Bhogal, New Delhi - 110014. M. That, the Hon'ble trial court overlooked the important fact that the great prejudice has been caused to the appellant/complainant as she has been forced to pay the rent of approx.. Rs. 15,000/- per month as per the impugned interim order. N. That, the Hon'ble trial court overlooked the important fact that the appellant/complainant has been deprived of her legal right of residence in the shared household/ matrimonial home (present) 0. That, the present appeal is bonafide which my kindly be considered in the interest of justice. In addition to the aforesaid grounds, Ld. Counsel for appellant/wife has argued that this appeal is arising out of the impugned order dated 30.06.2025 passed by Ld. Court of Ms. Neha Saini, JMFC (Mahila Court-02), Saket Court, New Delhi in Ct. Case No. 1055/2022, whereby Respondant No.1 was directed to pay a sum of Rs.10000/- per month (Rupees Ten Thousand only) to the Appellant for the Appellant (inclusive of food, clots, shelter, education and health from the date of filing of application towards interim maintenance. It is argued that the respondent no.1 & 2 along with the applicant/complainant and her daughter and son were residing in the rented house No.29, Ground floor, Bazar Lane, Jangpura, Bhogal, New Delhi - 110004 till the passing of the interim order. The rent of this house is approx. Rs. 18,000/- per month. That vide order dated 01-07-2022 passed by Ms. Tarunpreet kaur, the then Ld. MM/ Mahila Court-02/SED, Saket Court New Delhi was pleased to restrain the respondents from dispossessing CA No. 265/2025 Charanpreet Kaur vs. Parvinder Charanpreet Kaur vs Parvinder Singh on 7 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127053166/ 5 Singh & anr. Page no. 8 of 19 the appellant /complainant from the shared household/matrimonial home. That the respondent no.1 purchased 3 flats in the Property No. 3/31, First floor, Double Storey, DDA Flats, Near Mother Dairy, Opp. Kashmiri Park, Jangpura Extension, Bhogal, New Delhi - 110014 in the name of respondent no.2 Smt. Surjeet Kaur (Mother) when the son of the applicant/complainant was near about 10-12 years old. The respondent no. 1 was/is using the above said purchased flats as guest rooms by renting on daily/ monthly basis to the guests. That after passing of interim maintenance by the Hon'ble Court on dated 30-06- 2025 to avoid payment of arrears of interim maintenance & other liabilities the respondents left the applicant/complainant, her daughter and have shifted their luggage on 28.7.2025 to the property No. 3/31, First floor, Double Storey, DDA Flats, Near Mother Dairy, Opp. Kashmiri Park, Jangpura Extension, Bhogal, New Delhi - 110014, which is matrimonial home/shared household. That the landlord has asked the applicant/complainant to vacate the house.
texts.arguments: It has CA No. 265/2025 Charanpreet Kaur vs. Parvinder Singh & anr. Page no. 9 of 19 been argued the respondent currently is taking care of the old age mother Smt. Surjeet Singh and his son and also paying for the expenses of the education of his son by earning and working for the whole family. It has been argued that the respondent is unable to pay separate amount for the tenanted premises to the complainant and is ready and willing to abide by the order of the Ld. Trial Court and in compliance of the same has been paying the interim maintenance to the appellant being his wife. 8. On the other hand, it has been argued on behalf of the appellant that the Ld. Trial Court misapplied judicial precedent and ignored the legislative intent of the PWDV Act. Section 23 of the PWDV Act aims to provide immediate relief to prevent destitution during the main petition. The Ld. Trial Court's hyper-technical approach defeats this objective. That the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that depriving the appellant of the "shared household" is a grave act of domestic violence. As the legally wedded wife, she has an indefeasible right to reside there. Her forcible ouster on 19.05.2022 is a continuing act of domestic violence. Denial of maintenance to a woman unlawfully dispossessed is unjust. Granting monetary relief is necessary to protect her right to residence and sustenance. Section 20 of the DV Act stipulates that a Magistrate hearing an application under Section 12 of the DV Act may direct Respondent to pay certain monetary relief to the aggrieved person. It further delineates the contours of monetary relief that is to be paid to aggrieved person, including the criteria governing it as well as the manner in which the payment is to be made. For the ease of comprehension, Section 20 of the DV Act has been reproduced as under :- "20. Monetary reliefs (1)While disposing of an application under sub-section (1) of section 12, the Magistrate may direct the respondent to pay monetary relief to meet the expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any child of the aggrieved person as a result of the domestic violence and such relief may include, but not limited to, (a)the loss of earnings; (b)the medical expenses; (c)the loss caused due to the destruction, damage or removal of any property from the control of the aggrieved person; and (d)the maintenance for the aggrieved person as well as her children, if any, including an order under or in addition to an order of maintenance under section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974) or any other law for the time being in force. (2)The monetary relief granted under this section shall be adequate, fair and reasonable and consistent with the CA No. 265/2025 Charanpreet Kaur vs. Parvinder Singh & anr. Page no. 11 of 19 standard of living to which the aggrieved person is accustomed." 11. Where a woman is subjected to cruelty by her husband or her relatives for demand of dowry, it is an offence u/sec. 498A of the Indian Penal Code. We may also see that where an alternative constructions are possible, the court must give effect to that which will be responsible for the smooth working of the system for which the Charanpreet Kaur vs Parvinder Singh on 7 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127053166/ 7 statute has been enacted rather than the one which would put hindrances in its way. If the choice is between two CA No. 265/2025 Charanpreet Kaur vs. Parvinder Singh & anr. Page no. 12 of 19 interpretations, the narrower of which would fail to achieve the manifest purpose of the legislation, we should avoid a construction which would reduce the legislation to futility. 12. The Act inter-alia provides for more effective protection or the right of woman guaranteed under the constitution who are victims of the domestic violence of any kind occurring within the shared household. According to the Act, any harm, injury to health, safety, life, limb or well being or any other act or threatening or coercion etc. by any adult member of the family, constitutes domestic violence. Further, the act also contemplates that any woman who is or has been in a domestic relationship, if she is subjected to any domestic violence can file a complaint u/sec. 12 of the PWDV Act. This Act also covers those woman who are or have been in relationship with the abuser where both parties have live together in a shared household and a relative by consanguinity, marriage or through a relationship in the nature of marriage or adoption. During the course of arguments, both the parties even explored to look for an CA No. 265/2025 Charanpreet Kaur vs. Parvinder Singh & anr. Page no. 13 of 19 accommodation for the appellant and her daughter but were unable to reach at any conclusion and therefore, the arguments on merits were heard. For computing the maintenance, the following test have been laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Jasbir Kaur Sehgal vs. District Judge, Dehradun & Ors. 1997 (7) SCC 7, wherein it has been observed that: "No set formula can be laid for fixing the amount of maintenance. It has, in the very nature of things, to depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. Some scope for leverage can, however, be always there. The court has to consider the status of parties, their respective needs, the capacity of husband to pay having regard to his reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and of those he is obliged under the law and statutory but involuntary payments or deductions. The amount of maintenance fixed for wife or children should be such as she can live in reasonable comfort considering her status and the mode of life she was used to when she lived with her husband and also that she does not feel handicapped in the prosecution of her case. At the same time, the amount so fixed cannot be excessive or extortionate." 16. Further, Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Rajnesh Vs Neha & Anr, Crl. Appeal No. 730/2020 (arising out of SLP (Crl) No. 9503/2018, dated 04.11.2020 has held as under :- Criteria for determining quantum of maintenance :- The objective of granting interim / permanent alimony is to ensure that the dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or vagrancy on account of the failure of the CA No. 265/2025 Charanpreet Kaur vs. Parvinder Singh & anr. Page no. 15 of 19 marriage, and not as a punishment to the other spouse. There is no straitjacket formula for fixing the quantum of maintenance to be awarded. The factors which would weigh with the Court inter alia are the status of the parties; reasonable needs of the wife and dependent children; whether the applicant is educated and professionally qualified; whether the applicant has any independent source of income; whether the income is sufficient to enable her to maintain the same standard of living as she was accustomed to in her matrimonial home; whether the applicant was employed prior to her marriage; whether she was working during the subsistence of the marriage; whether the wife was required to sacrifice her employment opportunities for nurturing the family, child rearing, and looking after adult members of the family; reasonable costs of litigation for a nonworking wife. 17. Besides that, the court must take into consideration the status of the parties and the capacity of the spouse to pay for her or her child or his support, the financial capacity of the husband, his actual income, reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and dependent family members including his own child, whom he is obliged to maintain under the law, liabilities if any, would be required to be taken into consideration. The Court must have due regard to the standard of living of the husband, as well as the spiraling inflation rates and high costs of living. Charanpreet Kaur vs Parvinder Singh on 7 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127053166/ 9 CA No. 265/2025 Charanpreet Kaur vs. Parvinder Singh & anr. Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Rajnesh Vs Neha & Anr (Supra) has held as under :- (c) Where wife is earning some income. The Courts have held that if the wife is earning, it cannot operate as a bar from being awarded maintenance by the husband. The Courts have provided guidance on this issue in the following judgments. 19. Further, in order to determine the quantum of maintenance payable to an applicant, the Court shall take into account the criteria enumerated in Part B - III of the judgment Rajnesh Vs Neha and Anr. (supra). The objective of granting interim / permanent alimony is to ensure that the dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or vagrancy on account of the failure of the marriage, and not as a punishment to the other spouse.
